units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 48:20">Targ. Y. Gen. XLVIII, 20</cite>.—
<cite ref="Gittin 57a:21">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite> … <he>כי הוה מתיליד י׳ ינוקתא וכ׳</he> whenever a male child was born, they used to plant a cedar, when a female, they planted &c.

<cite ref="Shabbat 134a:14">Sabb. 134ᵃ</cite> <he>האי י׳ דלית ליה וכ׳</he> an infant (to be circumcised on the Sabbath) for which no bandage has been prepared, v. <cite ref="H01005"><he>חָלוּק</he> I</cite>.—
<cite ref="Sukkah 56b:7">Succ. 56ᵇ</cite> (prov.) <he>שותא די׳ וכ׳</he> the child’s talk in the street is either the father’s or the mother’s (talk at home).
Snh. 110ᵇ (ref. to פתאים, Ps. CXVI, 6) … שכן קורין לי׳ פתיא for in the sea towns they call a child pathia.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 21a:11">B. Bath. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>כד מחית לי׳ וכ׳</he> when thou (as teacher) strikest a child, strike it only with a shoe-strap.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 21a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>לא ממטינן י׳ וכ׳</he> we must not let a child go to school from one place to another (but must provide a school for each place).—
Gen. R. s. 36, a. e. יַנִּיקָא; a. fr.—Pl. יָנוּקֵי. B. Bath. l. c. מקרי י׳ primary school teacher, v. דַּרְדְּקָא; a. fr.—Fem. יָנוּקְתָּא. Gitt. l. c., v. supra.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 3b">B. Bath. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>האי י׳</he> that maiden (of Hasmonean descent, Mariamne).
